stem: In a cricket match, Kamran scored all of his runs from boundaries: fours, worth 4 runs each, and sixes, worth 6 runs each. He hit 13 boundaries and scored 64 runs from them. The system \(f + s = 13\) and \(4f + 6s = 64\) models this, where \(f\) is the number of fours and \(s\) is the number of sixes. How many sixes did Kamran hit?
solution: Then \(2s = 12\) and \(s = 6\). (Check: 7 fours and 6 sixes give \(28 + 36 = 64\) runs.)
verify:
f, s = symbols('f s')
sol = solve([f + s - 13, 4*f + 6*s - 64], [f, s])
assert sol == {f: 7, s: 6}
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [sol[s]]
